Subject: FastHawke launch — preliminary quota uplift request and regional split

Hi Aisha,

Quick note from FastHawke: we’ve locked a soft launch date for May 12 and expect an initial peak of ~120 RPS for the first 48 hours from our US cohort, tapering to ~30 RPS steady state. We also have a small EU pilot (London) that will add ~12 RPS.

Our infra lead asked if Redwood can temporarily increase token quota/rate for the prod API during the launch window and provide a regional routing plan (US primary, fallback EU). We need guidance on expected cold-start latency, any batching/caching recommendations, and what an uplift request looks like operationally (SLA, committed throughput or temporary burst).

I attached our latest forecast (forecast_v2.xlsx) and a short diagram of traffic flow. Can we get a quick rundown of required product toggles or feature flags we should expect to coordinate on your side?

Thanks — Devon

Team — looping you in to triage the ask and outline a clear action plan for FastHawke’s soft launch. Key asks from Devon: temporary quota/rate uplift, regional routing (US primary, EU fallback), and product toggles (canary, kv-cache prewarm).

Can each of you reply with the following by EOD:
- Karthik: propose a concrete uplift number and whether we can support a burst vs committed reservation for May 12–14. Include recommended batching/caching settings from Product.
- David: what operational constraints do we have for a short-term US peak at ~120 RPS and EU fallback; can we provide SLAs or SLO guidance and what telemetry we need to monitor?
- Marissa: pricing/approval path for a temporary burst (who signs, timeline for rate table changes), and whether finance needs a PO.
- Olga: any compliance/contract flags for cross-region fallback or for adding temporary capacity?

I’ve attached the customer forecast they shared (forecast_v2.xlsx) and a short product asks doc (prod_asks.md). Devon — thanks, we’ll come back with a concrete plan by tomorrow.

-Aisha

Date: 2027-04-07T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FastHawke launch — preliminary quota uplift request and regional split

Quick read: the numbers look reasonable for a short window. My proposal:
- Temporary burst capacity: increase token/sec quota to handle 140 RPS equivalent (we size on token throughput; I mapped their forecast to ~950k tokens/min peak). This is a burst-only uplift for 48 hours (May 12 00:00 UTC — May 14 00:00 UTC).
- Can support a small committed reservation if they want predictable pricing: commit to 60% of peak (approx 570k tokens/min) for the month with reduced unit price.
- Product toggles: enable prefix KV prewarm for the main model route, turn on aggressive batching (batch window 30ms) for latency-sensitive calls, and enable request-level tracing.

Notes/risks:
- If they open concurrent streaming sessions per user, token consumption will rise faster than RPS. Need to confirm session model.
- EU fallback: we can set a passive fallback route, but cross-region egress will add latency; recommend keeping EU as failover unless they specifically want a local EU pool.

I attached a short sheet mapping their RPS->tokens in this thread (I included the mapping in forecast_v2.xlsx). If product signs off, we can stage the uplift as a feature flag scoped to their org id and the date window.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

Thanks — operational checklist and constraints below. TL;DR: we can deliver a 48-hour burst for the US region but need the feature-flag window and traffic cutover times at least 72 hours prior for infra prep.

Operational constraints and asks:
- Prep window: 72 hours for slotting GPU pools and KV prewarm work. Please confirm exact UTC window.
- Safety caps: we will apply a hard cap at 160 RPS equivalent for the uplift window to protect shared capacity.
- Observability: need org-level tracing enabled and a dedicated PagerDuty schedule for the window. Provide the contact for on-call.
- Canary: recommend a stepped ramp: 25% of expected load for first 30 minutes, 60% for next 30, then full cutover. Provide a canary rollback plan (route back to default model variant).
- Prewarm: KV cache warm will take ~45m for typical prefix sets; we can script prewarm if they provide keys/seed prompts.

Attachment: ingress_topology.png (diagram of routing), and I added a short ops checklist to prod_asks.md.

-David
